backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is given, change the pair-filter cutoff from d0 < 0.15 to d0 < 0.3. Fewer real contacts are then dropped after the jitter, and the repair step has less to shrink, which may help larger perturbations reach valid optima. Only this constant changes.
backlog.title: Wider neighbour cutoff in basin hopping

backlog.spec: After the main while loop in solve, run one extra SLSQP from the best packing with no jitter and with all pair constraints (not just pairs with gap below 0.15), maxiter 100 and ftol 1e-12, then repair and keep the result only if its sum is higher. Implement by adding two optional arguments to _solve_once (jitter sd, default 0.02, and gap cut-off, default 0.15) and calling it with 0 and infinity. This recovers the slack that the default ftol 1e-6 and the repair shrink leave, and is different from the rejected LP polish of slot 2 because radii and centres move together.
backlog.title: Full pair constraints for the last hop on the best

backlog.spec: For a fresh start, build the initial centres sequentially: place the first circle uniformly at random, then for each next circle draw 500 random candidate points in the square and keep the candidate whose distance to its nearest existing centre (including the walls) is largest. Use the resulting n centres as the SLSQP start with the usual initial radius. The seed controls all candidate draws. This gives a maximin-spread start that differs from Lloyd relaxation and from pure uniform sampling.
backlog.title: Greedy farthest-point sequential insertion start

backlog.spec: Keep a set of signatures for each finished local optimum, where the signature is the sorted radii rounded to 3 decimals together with the rounded sum of radii. When a new fresh start's result has a signature already in the set, do not treat it as a new candidate and instead spend the next start on a fresh random layout. Count duplicates and log nothing. This avoids wasting budget on repeatedly re-finding the same basin and keeps the restart loop otherwise unchanged. Use only numpy and the standard library.
backlog.title: Duplicate-aware restarts with a signature memory

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase, replace the SLSQP call on a perturbed packing with a sequential linear programme: at each of up to 30 iterations, linearise the pair-distance and wall constraints around the current centres and radii, maximise the sum of radii subject to the linearised constraints and a box trust region of half-width delta on the centre moves and radii moves (scipy.optimize.linprog with highs). Accept a step if the true packing remains feasible in the sense of the linearised constraints within 1e-9, otherwise shrink delta by half; grow delta by 1.5 after success. Return the final centres and repaired radii. Keep SLSQP for fresh starts.
backlog.title: Sequential LP with trust region as local solver in basin hopping

backlog.spec: After the time budget is used, take the best packing and try a few deterministic affine rescales of the centres about (0.5, 0.5), with factors 1.0, 1.001, 1.002, 1.005 and each mapped into the square with the required wall margin. For each candidate, recompute radii as the minimum of wall distances and half pairwise gaps, then keep the candidate with the largest valid sum of radii. This is a cheap final step that may recover slack left by the repair. It only runs in the last 0.2 seconds of the budget.
backlog.title: Gap-inflating rescale of the best packing

backlog.spec: In the fresh-start branch of _solve_once, change the maxiter of the common-radius SLSQP from 50 to 100 and name it as a module setting INIT_ITER = 100. Slot 7 showed that this stage is the largest single gain so far, yet its length was never tuned; a better-converged equal-circle start may give better final basins at the cost of somewhat fewer fresh starts. No other change.
backlog.title: Tune common-radius stage length

backlog.spec: In the start-is-not-None branch of _solve_once, replace the global Gaussian jitter of all centres with a local one: pick a random circle k with rng, find all circles whose centre is within 0.25 of centre k, and add normal(0, 0.05) noise only to those centres. All other centres stay exactly as in the best packing. Keep the clip to [0.01, 0.99] and the rest unchanged. The idea is that the best packing is near-optimal almost everywhere, so a strong local rearrangement is more likely to improve it than a weak global shake.
backlog.title: Local-patch jitter in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is given, replace the fixed Gaussian jitter sd of 0.02 with a per-circle sd of 0.4*r_i, where r_i is that circle's radius in the start packing. Use the same rng and keep the clip to [0.01,0.99]. Small circles, which sit in holes, then move a little, and large circles explore more. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-proportional jitter in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Pass a callback to scipy's SLSQP minimize call (or check the iterate inside the objective wrapper) that records the current sum of radii and the iteration count. If, after 25 iterations, the sum of radii is below 0.92 times the current best sum, raise a private exception that is caught in _solve_once and the partial iterate is returned for the repair step. Full runs are unchanged for promising starts. This saves time on bad basins without the separate screening stage used before.
backlog.title: Early abort of hopeless SLSQP runs via callback

backlog.spec: Replace the fresh-start initialisation with a simple event-free compression: start with random centres and tiny radius; for 30 iterations alternate (a) growing a common radius by 5 percent and (b) pushing overlapping pairs apart by half the overlap along their centre line, clipping to the square. Use the result as input to the main SLSQP with radii set to 0.9 of the common radius.
backlog.title: Compression start via growing radii

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, replace the uniform random centres in y0 with Mitchell best-candidate sampling: place the first point uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]^2; for each following point draw 10 uniform candidates in the same box with rng and keep the one whose minimum distance to the points already placed is largest. This costs a few hundred microseconds, gives well-spread but irregular starts (unlike the grid and hex lattices already tried), and should let the 50-iteration common-radius SLSQP converge further.
backlog.title: Best-candidate (blue-noise) initial centres

backlog.spec: Make no functional change to train.py: only reword the module docstring's first line (for example append 'Fresh starts, then basin hopping.') so the edit applies. The purpose is a third and fourth measurement of the incumbent, because nearly every later result is -2.9374 against an incumbent mean of -2.9366 and the per-job noise sd is 0.0034. Any later accept decision needs a tighter incumbent estimate.
backlog.title: No-op replicate of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping phase keep two chains: the global best and a second packing which is the best from a different fresh start (sum within 0.01 of best but different). Alternate basin-hopping steps between the chains; each chain replaces its own state only on improvement. Return the best overall.
backlog.title: Independent dual chains

backlog.spec: Make two changes together. First, for fresh starts only, before the common-radius SLSQP, run 20 steps of pairwise 1/d^2 repulsion on the random centres: force on i is the sum over j of (c_i-c_j)/|c_i-c_j|^3. Add a wall repulsion term too. Cap each step's per-circle displacement at 0.02 and clip the centres to [0.05,0.95]. Second, in the late phase (after 0.4*time_limit), keep a 'current' packing alongside the best. Perturb the current packing with the existing jitter (sd 0.02) and run SLSQP. Accept the new packing as current if its sum is higher, or with probability exp((new-cur)/0.002) otherwise. Update best whenever the sum improves. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Combine repulsion pre-step (slot 14) with Metropolis basin-hopping chain (slot 25)

backlog.spec: In _solve_once main SLSQP call, remove the four wall constraint blocks and the r>=0 block from cons, and pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Add the wall constraints back only as linear inequality via a small constraint function if needed for validity; _repair still clamps radii by wall distance so output stays valid. Fewer constraints should make each SLSQP iteration faster, allowing more restarts.
backlog.title: Wall constraints as variable bounds

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP call, rescale the decision vector so that coordinates live in [0,1] units and radii are multiplied by a constant of about 10 (for example, optimise u = (c, 10*r) and map back before returning). Pass the scaled objective and constraints so the gradient magnitudes of the centre and radius blocks are comparable. Keep the rest of the pipeline (restarts, repair, time limit) unchanged. The goal is to reduce SLSQP stalls on the radius block, which currently has entries near 0.09 while centres span about 1.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning

backlog.spec: For every second fresh start (alternate with a counter), replace the uniform random initial centres fed to the common-radius SLSQP with a greedy construction: draw 2000 candidate points uniformly in the unit square with rng; repeat n times: for each candidate compute the largest radius allowed by the walls and the circles already placed (min of wall distance and distance to placed centre minus its radius), pick the candidate with the largest allowed radius capped at a cap drawn from uniform(0.07, 0.12), and place it. Use the resulting centres as the first 2n entries of y0; the rest of _solve_once is unchanged.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole construction for fresh starts

backlog.spec: In the fresh-start branch, change the cheap init SLSQP so that circle i has radius t*w_i rather than a single shared radius t. The weights w_i are drawn once per start from rng.uniform(0.6,1.4). The constraints become dist_ij >= t*(w_i+w_j) and the wall constraints use t*w_i, and the problem still has only 2n+1 variables, maximising t. Initialise the main SLSQP with radii max(t*w_i, 0.01). This seeds unequal sizes while keeping the low-dimensional pre-solve that worked in slot 7.
backlog.title: Random-weighted common-radius init stage

backlog.spec: After each _solve_once returns centres c and radii, solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) maximizing sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance, r>=0, with centres fixed. Use these radii instead of SLSQP radii before the repair step (repair then only does a tiny shrink). This picks the best radii for each candidate when ranking restarts.
backlog.title: LP-optimal radii after each SLSQP

memo:
Helped: search-strategy changes only. Slot 4 (basin-hopping from jittered copies of the best packing after 40% of the time) gave -0.0050 over 2 runs. Slot 7 (cheap common-radius SLSQP init for fresh starts) gave -0.0063 over 2 runs. The incumbent is -2.9366, about 0.0004 below the published 2.9370, so little headroom remains.

Did not help: constraint reformulation (slot 0, +0.0140), analytic Jacobians (+0.0007), final polish (+0.0049), mirror starts (+0.0014), L-BFGS-B penalty init (+0.0056), per-circle random radii (+0.0081). Nearly all later single-run tweaks sit within noise (sd about 0.0034). The best were slots 14 and 25 (-0.0030 each) and slot 10 (-0.0020). Several were aborted as duplicates.

Next: replicate the incumbent first. Then replicate slots 14, 25 and 10 and try combining them. Avoid repeating tried ideas. Keep the code simple. Further gains are likely below the noise level, so consider stopping.
